Acids contain the other H, one hydrogen. These really like to join and form water, so they break away from the acid and base to react. In our case, baking soda is sodium bicarbonate (a base) and vinegar is diluted acetic acid. When they react to release the OH and H to become water. This makes the reaction bubble and expand, just like when you shake up a can of soda and open it!
